NEW FINDING (found live, NOT fixed, NOT authorized -- no-auto-fix rule): app/db/repositories/shop.repository.ts's upsertInstalledShop() cannot create a brand-new shop row -- ShopModel.installedAt (app/db/models/shop.model.ts) is allowNull:false with no defaultValue at the Sequelize model layer, only a DB-side DEFAULT now(); Sequelize's client-side validator rejects the insert before SQL is ever sent. Full detail and reproduction in dev-evidence/g4-sprint-2.1-m2-m3/00-SUMMARY.md. Neither file was touched by this sprint's diff. This blocks every real token-exchange install in production and should be the next authorized bug-fix command -- same severity class as the BUG-1/2/4/5 chain from G4-sprint-1.1. Does not block or invalidate this sprint's own evidence: no route built this sprint creates a shop row.

M4 (save/history persistence of a `calculation` row) is explicitly out of scope this sprint per the task brief -- the Calculate flow is a live, non-persisted preview only (app/domain/calculation-transport.ts). The `data-save-bar` form-attribute contextual-save-bar approach (app/routes/app.calculator.tsx) is confirmed against shopify.dev docs (Save Bar API / App Bridge web components) via the same Dev MCP conversation, but has not been exercised against a real embedded Admin session with actual App Bridge JS loaded -- VERIFY AT BUILD / at first real dev-store install that App Bridge actually auto-detects this form's dirty state and that the Save button's implicit form submission is captured correctly by the hidden intent field defaulting to "save".

SUPPORTED_CURRENCY_CODES (app/domain/expense-rule-validation.ts) hardcodes a 2-decimal minor-unit exponent for all 4 supported currencies (USD/CAD/EUR/GBP) -- correct for all four today, but flagged verify-at-build if a non-2-exponent currency (e.g. JPY, KWD) is ever added, per ADR-0005's general currency-exponent guidance.

MCP validation covers Polaris/App-Bridge component usage only (validate_component_codeblocks) -- it does not (and cannot) verify the calculation engine's money/rounding correctness; that is proven separately by the vitest determinism/reconciliation/tie-break tests and the live-evidence.ts run against a real database, both referenced above.
